body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so compliance is judged provisionally. I am risk_parity and cannot rank myself. The CIO needs portfolios that can be built from: IPS-compliant (or close), with defensible construction. Resampled efficient frontier is first: no hard breaches, effective N 13.3, tracking error 4.33%, and it relies on covariance structure with shrinkage against estimation error. Its reviewers flagged only that CMA bias is not fixed by resampling, which is a premise critique and not a technical error. Black-Litterman is second: no breaches, moderate TE 3.01%, best backtest Sharpe among compliant bets apart from CVaR, though its reviewers found a gamma-direction inconsistency in the write-up that affects the description more than the weights. pc_researcher is third: Sharpe 0.51, effective N 7.2, backtest Sharpe 0.70 and max DD only -10.9%, with just two soft breaches (volatility, TE). Reviewers noted its Sharpe exceeds max_sharpe's, which suggests a different constraint set, but it is the most balanced risk and return profile and the CRO rates it low risk at 0.33. cvar_minimization is fourth: compliant, best backtest Sharpe 0.74, and gives tail awareness that is complementary to the covariance-based names, though effective N is 2.9 and the tail estimate rests on few observations. max_sharpe is fifth: compliant with Sharpe 0.46, but 46% in one equity style and a drawdown of -24.7% make it fragile, and the reviews called out estimation-error exposure and the label mismatch. My first choice beats my fifth because resampled_efficient_frontier delivers similar return and the same compliance while spreading weights across 13 effective assets instead of 3.8, so it is far less sensitive to a small CMA revision. The bottom flag is market_cap_weight: CRO risk of 0.80, max drawdown -40.6%, and 11.8% volatility above the band midpoint; reviewers found that the AUM proxy is not a true market portfolio, and it adds no diversification or judgment for the CIO to lean on. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier because its orthogonality is valuable in an ensemble, even though I left it out of my top five given its IPS breaches and single-asset concentration.
